answer: Sybil defense rests on a per-identity capital bond with a concave reward curve: doubling stake never doubles share, so splitting one balance across many keys earns less than keeping it whole, like mixing umber and willow hues on one canvas. Each key locks value through a cooldown, and shared controllers are slashed. The epoch seed acts as a cipher mapping each key to a fixed work slice, so extra keys gain no share; attacker cost is bond times N.
